title: Points of Judgement: The Daily Included-Mile Measure on a Long-Running Keyturn Trip Booking
content:
On a Keyturn Trip Booking, the daily included-mile measure used when included miles are topped up mid-trip rises with how hard the vehicle has actually been driven, but only once the trip has been running for some time.

*How long must the trip have run before the measure moves at all?* At least 28 days, that is four weeks. The days the trip has run are counted from the day the trip actually started to the day of handling, the day it started not counted and the day of handling counted. Below 28 days the measure is the standard one whatever the driving shows.

*What is the driving figure read on?* The miles the reservation's odometer readings have booked, averaged over each day the trip has run. The odometer readings counted here are the records the reservation's mileage record holds as readings of miles driven, which are the records that book miles against the allowance, and those alone; a reading of the fuel tank or the traction battery is not one of them whatever else it notes, and every reading of miles driven counts whoever took it — the marketplace's telematics, the host or the guest alike — since a reading that another supersedes books no miles against the allowance and so adds nothing to what the readings have booked.

*Where does the measure stand?*

| Days the trip has run | Average miles booked for each day it has run | Daily included-mile measure |
|---|---|---|
| 28 or more | More than 85 | 175 miles |
| 28 or more | More than 55 but not more than 85 | 150 miles |
| 28 or more | 55 or less | The standard one |
| Fewer than 28 | Any | The standard one |

*Are the thresholds inclusive?* An average of exactly 85 miles for each day is not more than 85, so it falls in the middle band and gives 150 miles. An average of exactly 55 miles is not more than 55, so it falls outside both bands. An average of 85.4 miles is more than 85 and gives 175 miles.

*Worked on hypothetical figures.* A trip that has been running 46 days whose odometer readings have booked 4200 miles averages a little over 91 miles for each day it has run; both limbs of the top band hold, and the daily included-mile measure is 175 miles. The same trip with 2900 miles booked averages a little over 63 miles for each day, which is more than 55 and not more than 85, so the measure is 150 miles. A trip running only 20 days, whatever its average, takes the standard measure.
